# V3 lane map and task map {#sec-appg}

This appendix has two parts. The lane map says which V3 design lane owns each part of the code, which design
document describes it, where that code lives at the pin, and which chapters of this book cover it. The task map
lists each task a reader wants to do with snapy and the section that answers it, or the reason the book does not.

## V3 lanes and design documents {.unnumbered .unlisted}

V3 was designed in lanes. Each lane has one design document, whose sections 3 (target design) and 4 (register
contract) are its contract, and a skeleton of declarations under `docs/v3/skeleton/<lane>/` on its branch, in no
build.[^appg-design] @tbl-appg-lanes lists the nine lanes with the classes that carry each one at the code pin
and the chapters that describe them. The chapter numbers are those of the outline; a chapter not yet written at
the pin may still carry the title it had before the outline.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Find the design document, the code and the chapters of a V3 lane.

**Data.** The lane table of the V3 design summary (scope, document, skeleton), the code at the pin, and the
chapter plan of the report outline.

**Placement.** Report preparation, outside the solver.

**Activation.** None; hand-written, with each code entry cited by symbol and checked at the pin by
`code_anchors.py`.

**Guarantee / limits.** Each named class or function exists at the pin; a lane's design document may describe
more than the pin implements.

**Evidence.** `tools/code_anchors.py check` resolves every code entry of @tbl-appg-lanes.
:::

: The V3 lanes: scope and design document from the V3 design summary, the classes that carry each lane at the
code pin, and the chapters that describe it. {#tbl-appg-lanes}

Three pieces of closing work cut across the lanes. B3 (multi-block capture, exchange cuts and the Mesh's
agreement on capture) is described in @sec-ch11 and @sec-ch13. S4 (the eager-path launch reduction) is spread
over the chapters that own the kernels it changed (@sec-ch04, @sec-ch06, @sec-ch09 and @sec-ch10), with its cost
catalogue in @sec-ch11 and its counting method in @sec-ch16. The capture rules, allow-lists and the capture sweep
are @sec-ch11 and @sec-ch16. Chapters 1, 16 and 17 and appendix J draw on every lane.[^appg-outline]

## Reader tasks {.unnumbered .unlisted}

Each task a reader wants to do with snapy is listed here once, under what the book says about it: answered,
partly documented, undocumented, unsupported by the code, or outside the scope of this report. An answered or
partly documented task names the section that answers it; a partly documented answer leaves part of the task
open, and that section says which part. A task the book does not answer gives the reason instead.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Find the section that answers a "How do I ...?" task, or why the book does not.

**Data.** `tools/reader-tasks.md`: one row per task, seeded from the newcomer question bank, tasks
readers could not find, the extension blocks and the DO cards, with the answering section or a reason.

**Placement.** Report preparation, outside the solver.

**Activation.** Run `gen_reader_tasks.py`; no solver switch.

**Guarantee / limits.** Every row names the labelled section that answers it, never a whole chapter, or a reason;
a status records the lookup grade, not a code audit.

**Evidence.** `tools/tests/test_reader_tasks.py` fails on a section that does not exist, on a chapter target and
on a missing reason; the rendered gate checks every destination in the PDF build.
:::
